name: PG4
summary: PG4 is Pfizer's fourth-generation pneumococcal conjugate vaccine, PF-07872412 (25vPnC). It is the Prevnar 20 backbone plus serotypes 15A, 23A, 23B, 24F and 35B. It is identified from the trials: the Phase 2 NCT06524414 is Pfizer's 25vPnC infant study (pfizerclinicaltrials.com/nct06524414-pneumococcal-disease-trial). The pivotal infant safety study NCT07573462 matches the May 2026 announcement of a 2,400-child Phase 3 against Prevnar 20 at 2, 4, 6 and 12-15 months. The lead Phase 3 is the infant immunogenicity study NCT07629440 (3,230 infants, primary completion 2029-06-05). Price anchor: Prevnar 20 pediatric at the CDC private-sector price of $299.25 a dose, $1,197 for four doses, the anchor the book's PCV21 seed uses. Uptake anchor: Prevnar 20's measured class sweep (83.0% of CMS conjugate doses in its first full year) as the ceiling for a franchise successor, cut to the share the book's PCV21 seed leaves. This revenue largely replaces Prevnar 20 pediatric revenue that the book already carries on the Prevnar family seed. Adding PG4 on top without eroding that seed double-counts it.

therapy_mode.source: NCT07573462 / Pfizer press release 2026-05-20 (https://www.pfizer.com/news/press-release/press-release-detail/pfizer-advances-pivotal-pediatric-pneumococcal-vaccine): four-dose infant series at 2, 4, 6 and 12-15 months
therapy_mode.note: A single infant course, billed once per child on an annual birth cohort. The book's PCV21 seed models it the same way

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py seed PCV21: Prevnar 20 pediatric, CDC Pediatric/VFC price list of June 2026, private sector $299.25 a dose x 4 = $1,197
list_price_per_patient.note: A published list price for the incumbent this vaccine replaces, which beats the CMS convention (CMS Part B Prevnar 20 spend is adult only). The case against: Pfizer took a price step from Prevnar 13 to Prevnar 20, and a 25-valent successor will likely be priced above $299.25. No PG4 price exists, so no premium is applied. I did not re-open the CDC price list myself; the figure is the book's

gross_to_net_pct.source: lookup.py seed PCV21: 52.2% of US children VFC-eligible at the federal contract price of $200.13 against $299.25 private (MMWR 2024;73(33) Vital Signs). Realised price 0.522 x 200.13 + 0.478 x 299.25 = $247.51, 82.71% of list
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: 17.29% off list, so the net course is $990. Reused from the book because it is the same population and payer mix. The case against: the blend ignores private-sector rebates and any CDC stockpile pricing, so the true share off list is likely a little higher

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: brief convention for a fixed course: the infant series is completed and not repeated
discontinuation_pct.note: Moot under one_time; set to 1.0 so no stock carries forward if the engine reads it

forecast_start_year.source: NCT07629440 primary completion 2029-06-05; NCT07573462 primary completion 2028-12-30 (ClinicalTrials.gov, per the context file)
forecast_start_year.note: Judgement on the timeline. Infant immunogenicity reads out mid-2029, a BLA follows in late 2029, and a standard 10 to 12 month biologics review gives approval in the second half of 2030. An ACIP recommendation and VFC contract are then needed before the cohort switches, so 2031 is the first full year

exus_multiple.source: Prevnar family FY2025: $2,342mm International against $4,151mm US (Pfizer 10-K 0000078003-26-000026, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/78003/000007800326000026/pfe-20251231.htm; Q4 2025 earnings release)
exus_multiple.note: Judgement on the comparator. It is the franchise this vaccine succeeds, but the split mixes adult and pediatric sales, and Pfizer does not file a pediatric-only split. The case for higher: the 10-K credits new pediatric launches in emerging markets. The case against: ex-US pediatric tenders are price-driven, and a 25-valent vaccine may not displace cheaper PCV13 and PCV20 in tender markets

economics_share.source: Pfizer is lead sponsor of NCT07629440, NCT07573462, NCT07660198, NCT07794748 and NCT06524414. The Prevnar franchise is wholly owned, and the 2026-05-20 press release names no partner
economics_share.note: No partner found. I did not check a filing for a royalty

prevalence.source: carried by the book: 3,628,934 US births in 2024 (NVSR 75-02), on the PCV21 vaccine seed (lookup.py pool Pneumococcal)
prevalence.note: Carried by the book. It is the infant birth cohort, which is the lead Phase 3 population. The adult (NCT07794748) and catch-up (NCT07660198) studies are not modelled, because this pool is a birth cohort and a second pool under the same name is forbidden

incidence.source: carried by the book: set equal to the birth cohort on the PCV21 seed

eligible_pct.source: 80.5% of US children complete four or more pneumococcal conjugate doses (MMWR 2026;75(11):146-155), the figure the PCV21 seed carries
eligible_pct.note: Reused so the two pediatric PCV assets share one eligible pool. I did not independently re-open the MMWR

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the cohort's completed courses
penetration_peak_pct.source: Anchor: Prevnar 20 took 82.999% of the 1,509,155 CMS conjugate class in 2022, its first full year, rising to 96.588% in 2024 (the PCV21 seed's measurement from lookup.py demand). Cut to 1 - 0.2075, the share left after the book's PCV21 vaccine seed takes 20.75% of the same cohort
penetration_peak_pct.note: Judgement. A Pfizer successor inherits the incumbent franchise, as Prevnar 20 did from Prevnar 13, so its measured first-year sweep is the anchor. It is capped at the residual so that the two pediatric PCV seeds under this indication do not sum above 100% of the cohort. The uncut 0.83 would sum to 1.04. The case against: the anchor is adult Medicare data, and pediatric switching runs through ACIP and VFC contracts. Merck (Vaxneuvance and successors) and Vaxcyte (VAX-31) compete for the pediatric slot. Any of these could hold PG4 well below this

ramp_steepness.source: lookup.py seed PCV21: lower-quartile fit over the 41 measured launches in data/launch_ramp.csv
ramp_steepness.note: Reused from the closest modelled competitor. The case against: Prevnar 20 reached 83% of its class within its first full year, so a same-franchise successor could ramp much faster than this curve
